First reasoned review, 2026-10-20

All verdicts derive from source or recovered execution paths. ML scores and
provided external flags were leads. The two linked Triage reports could not be
retrieved. No external report is used as execution evidence below. No sample was
executed. Deployment context and operator authorization are unavailable.

68beeebf2c1b9d54b635cf55d12f57b99050f065a28c29e54e299e16236ef433
Identification: Linux userspace kernel-thread impostor / cron installer.
Verdict: MALICIOUS.
The complete 415-byte source calls prctl(PR_SET_NAME, "[kworker/u:8:0]"),
opens root's crontab spool in append mode, writes a five-minute job executing
/root/.local/share/.gvfsd/gvfsd-user, closes it, then waits forever in pause().
It neither creates that payload nor checks that cron accepted the entry.
Root access, a compatible cron spool, and the external payload are prerequisites.
A deliberately false kernel-thread identity combined with hidden root cron
execution tips the judgment; no legitimate maintenance purpose is evidenced.
Coverage retained: three suspicious traits, including masquerade and cron
persistence. No hostile trait is invented for the absent payload.

c215e2e0512237d2428926071a0c78f4c20f838903a05fd05441f3a785b1ed29
Identification: custom .NET NanoCoreUltimate.Program, original filename
"thearcane.com_nano.exe". This is not proof of authentic NanoCore or HiddenTear
family membership. Its many malware-family words do not establish identities.
Verdict: MALICIOUS.
Recovered all managed method bodies with dnfile/dncil and resolved metadata
calls. Entry token 0x06000085 is Main, RVA 0x7bd4. Main directly invokes
security-control sabotage, hosts poisoning, shadow deletion, IFEO modification,
self-replication, persistence and StartKeylogger; Task.Run delegates invoke
clipboard/screen/file collection and other helpers. Application.Run keeps the
keyboard hook alive. HookCallback records WM_KEYDOWN keys and active-window
names in a StringBuilder; FlushKeylog serializes the buffer to SendToC2.
Clipboard state machine reads Unicode clipboard data, screenshots use
CopyFromScreen and JPEG serialization, and file collection reads selected user
files. Browser methods read Chromium Login Data and Firefox logins.json, and
wallet methods read wallet files; no password decryption is implemented there.
Wi-Fi collection launches netsh wlan show profiles and key=clear profile queries.

Execution limits materially narrow claims:
* ParseC2Url (RVA 0x28c0) unconditionally stores an empty domain. IsPlaceholder
  (0x2910) unconditionally returns true. SendToC2 (0x30c8) first appends data to
  desktop and temporary logs, then its gate bypasses HTTP. Outbound theft to the
  named domain is not established. Existing hostile collection traits are
  appropriate; the network exfiltration composite remains absent.
* RealEncryption's MoveNext (0x5208) targets Desktop/TestFolder and attempts
  read -> EncryptAES -> suffixed WriteAllBytes -> original Delete. EncryptAES
  assigns a 16-byte key and a 14-byte IV. Aes.set_IV should throw before output
  or deletion. The trait correctly says file-replacement attempt, not successful
  encryption or filesystem-wide ransomware damage.
* DumpLSASS opens an LSASS handle and logs access; it does not dump credentials.
  Injection includes a RET-only payload and a small demonstration hollowing
  payload. API references do not establish a functioning injected RAT.
* CorruptSystemFiles (0x7818) combines the System directory with kernel32.dll,
  ntdll.dll and user32.dll. CIL offset 0x66 supplies FileMode.Append (6) and
  FileAccess.Write (2); a 1024-byte array is filled by Random.NextBytes and
  written to that FileStream. It appends, rather than overwriting PE headers.
  A broken DLL or boot failure is not established; file protections may deny it.

Actual surveillance and the unconditional attempts to disable security/recovery
controls justify MALICIOUS despite disabled C2 and defective encryption. There
is no evidence of a consent or containment boundary around those effects.
Added neutral append-buffer traits. Corrected the
NextBytes atom's description to describe name evidence, not a proven call.
Existing 24 hostile and 16 suspicious findings remain supported.

9e89865032e1c045c73e67f3018d6001c54999f9a4a4ef364953e60a5dec5c71
Identification: native x86 StormAttack resource DLL loader, memory-dump-like PE.
Verdict: MALICIOUS.
Rizin analysis and PE parsing show raw section offsets equal RVAs, resolved
IAT addresses, extra memory-like sections and an entirely zeroed 40 KiB .rsrc.
Entry 0x402674 reaches the loader entry routine at 0x401cb0.
* 0x402460 extracts resource 101 of type DLL; 0x4023c0 writes it to disk.
* 0x401150 starts a host process, allocates remote memory, writes a DLL path,
  resolves kernel32!LoadLibraryA and passes that address and remote path to
  CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
* 0x401260 opens LanmanServer\\Parameters, deletes ServiceDLL, and sets a new
  expandable-string DLL value. These are actual call sites, not just imports.
* Configuration mode 3 selects 0x401900: a generated component key under Active
  Setup receives StubPath; the executable is read, patched and written to a
  new path using CRT file I/O, then launched. Alternate modes install a service
  or invoke DLL injection.
* 0x401390 builds COMSPEC /c del <own-short-path> > nul and launches it.
The family banner pair and implementation corroborate StormAttack identity;
resource injection, persistence and cleanup tip the malicious judgment.

This copy's zeroed resource directory causes FindResource to fail; the loader
returns before the downstream drop, injection and persistence branches. Existing
traits accurately describe surviving code, not successful infection. There is
no basis to call the appended SQLite/runtime memory a functional ransomware
payload or assert a working DDoS engine in this artifact.

The old "pinned external IPv4 host" finding is 3.8.10.2 in an SQLite table beside
THREADSAFE=1 and SYSTEM_MALLOC. A dotted quad alone cannot distinguish a version
from an address. Renamed that atom and every YAML reference to
external-ipv4-shaped-text-binary, with an explicit version caveat. Matching,
criticality and consumer membership are preserved; no whole-file library
exception hides other addresses. Existing four hostile traits remain supported.

Verification
atomscan and cleave facts ran on each original, followed by atomscan rescans.
All after-edit scans retain the required hostile/suspicious coverage. The
renamed IPv4 atom is the only removed old ID. The managed sample gains the two
append profile observations. Other native findings and all C findings are
unchanged. A redundant new Windows DLL-name trait was removed after it
increased four benign fixture scores; existing references cover that evidence.

check.py accepts the original managed/native samples and builds seven temporary
controls. The append profile survives token changes, but fails when Append is
replaced by Open or FileStream/NextBytes metadata is absent. The IPv4 shape
matcher accepts a public-address control and rejects private/invalid controls.
These controls test detector evidence, not whether the modified samples execute.
